record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Clarify the nature of the renormalized perturbation series for four-dimensional φ⁴ theory, including proving that renormalons really occur.

evidence.quote: Elucidate the nature of φ4 4 renormalized pertubation series, proving for instance that renormalons do exist

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider four-dimensional Euclidean scalar field theory with quartic self-interaction, formally defined by the Lagrangian
  L(φ) = (1/2)(∂φ)² + (1/2) m² φ² + (λ/4!) φ⁴,
on R⁴, with bare parameters chosen so that, after BPHZ (or any equivalent) renormalization, the perturbation series for the connected Schwinger functions
  S_N^ren(x₁,…,x_N; λ) = Σ_{n≥0} a_n(x₁,…,x_N) λⁿ
is well defined order by order.

Carry out a rigorous analysis of this renormalized perturbation series. In particular:

(a) Determine the large-order asymptotic behavior of the coefficients a_n and identify the dominant singularities of the Borel transform
  B(t) = Σ_{n≥0} a_n tⁿ/n!
in the complex Borel plane.

(b) Prove the existence of renormalon singularities, i.e., establish rigorously that B(t) possesses singularities on the positive real axis arising from chains of self-energy or vertex insertions in Feynman graphs whose number of renormalization subtractions grows linearly with the order n, and locate the leading such singularity.

(c) Characterize the resulting obstruction to Borel summability of the full (non-planar) renormalized perturbation series for φ⁴ in four dimensions, and clarify in what precise analytic sense the series represents (or fails to represent) a non-perturbative Euclidean field theory.
artifact.status_search_result: The rigorous existence of renormalons in four-dimensional φ⁴ theory remains an open problem. While Borel summability has been established in restricted settings (planar φ⁴₄ by 't Hooft, Rivasseau, and others, and infrared φ⁴₄ via phase-space expansions), the full proof that renormalon singularities genuinely occur on the positive Borel axis of the complete renormalized perturbation series has not been achieved. Recent work (e.g., 2025 analyses of mean-field φ⁴₄) continues to address related aspects but does not settle the question.

status_evidence.title: Construction and Borel summability of planar 4-dimensional euclidean field theory
status_evidence.snippet: Planar part of renormalized perturbation theory for φ⁴₄ is Borel-summable on the asymptotically free side; renormalon singularities in the planar world are discussed.
status_evidence.claim: Borel summability is known only for the planar sector; full renormalon structure of φ⁴₄ is not rigorously established.

status_evidence.title: On the large order behavior of φ⁴_4
status_evidence.snippet: Even in the presence of renormalons, the Borel transform of perturbation has a finite radius of convergence.
status_evidence.claim: Large-order behavior is partially controlled, but rigorous existence of renormalon singularities is not proven.

status_evidence.title: Triviality vs perturbation theory: an analysis for mean-field φ⁴-theory in four dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work analyzing mean-field φ⁴₄ perturbation theory.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research on perturbative structure of φ⁴₄ indicates the question is still active.
